summary.goal: Enable planning agents to connect to Planner's MCP server and use planning tools to modify plans
summary.context: The MCP server already exists (src/mcp/server.ts) with stdio transport. For relay agents, we need a transport that allows remote connection. Agents spawned via relay-pty need to connect back and call tools like read_plan, add_step, edit_step, etc.

acceptance_criteria.description: MCP server supports HTTP transport (POST /mcp/tools/list, POST /mcp/tools/call)
Planning agent can list available tools
Planning agent can call any MCP tool
Tool calls result in SQLite database changes
Authentication via session token for MCP connections
Optimistic locking prevents edit conflicts

steps.title: Add HTTP transport to MCP server
steps.description: Extend src/mcp/server.ts to support HTTP transport in addition to stdio. Add POST /mcp/tools/list and POST /mcp/tools/call endpoints.

acceptance_criteria.description: POST /mcp/tools/list returns { tools: [{ name, description, inputSchema }] }
POST /mcp/tools/call accepts { name: string, arguments: object } and returns { result: any, error?: string }
Same tool handlers used for both stdio and HTTP transports

steps.title: Add session context to tool calls
steps.description: Modify tool call handler to accept session context (plan_id, agent_id) from authenticated session. Ensure agent can only modify the plan it's assigned to.

acceptance_criteria.description: Tool calls include session context from auth token: { plan_id, agent_id, session_id }
Agent scoped to its assigned plan - cannot modify other plans
read_plan without plan_id uses session's plan_id

steps.title: Add authentication for MCP connections
steps.description: Generate session token when agent spawned (from relay-planning-agent). Agent must include token in MCP requests via Authorization header. Validate token on each request.

acceptance_criteria.description: Session token generated on spawn, stored in sessions table
Requests without valid Authorization: Bearer <token> rejected with 401
Token passed to agent via MCP_SESSION_TOKEN environment variable
Token lookup returns { plan_id, agent_id, session_id, expires_at }

steps.title: Add optimistic locking for concurrent edits
steps.description: Add version check to edit operations. If human edited since agent last read, agent must re-read before editing. Prevents overwrite conflicts.

acceptance_criteria.description: Edit tools (edit_step, add_step, remove_step) accept optional expected_version parameter
Conflict returns { error: 'VERSION_CONFLICT', current_version: number, expected_version: number }
Agent re-reads plan state on conflict before retrying
read_plan returns version number in response

steps.title: Add tests for MCP bridge
steps.description: Write integration tests: spawn mock agent, call MCP tools via HTTP, verify database changes, verify auth and locking.

acceptance_criteria.description: Tests verify tool calls work via HTTP transport
Tests verify auth enforcement (401 without token)
Tests verify session scoping (cannot modify other plans)
Tests verify optimistic locking (conflict detection)

cases.description: POST /mcp/tools/list returns array of tools with name, description, inputSchema
POST /mcp/tools/call with valid tool name and arguments returns { result }
add_step via HTTP transport creates step in database
edit_step via HTTP transport updates step in database
remove_step via HTTP transport deletes step from database
read_plan via HTTP transport returns plan state
Session token generated on agent spawn and stored in sessions table
Valid Authorization: Bearer <token> header allows request
Token lookup returns { plan_id, agent_id, session_id, expires_at }
Tool calls receive session context from authenticated token
read_plan without plan_id arg uses session's plan_id
edit_step with correct expected_version succeeds
read_plan returns version number in response
Same tool handlers work for both stdio and HTTP transports
Tool call for session's assigned plan succeeds
edit_step without expected_version still works (backward compatible)
Expired token rejected with 401
POST /mcp/tools/call without Authorization header returns 401
POST /mcp/tools/call with invalid token returns 401
POST /mcp/tools/call with unknown tool name returns { error: 'TOOL_NOT_FOUND' }
POST /mcp/tools/call with invalid arguments returns { error: 'INVALID_ARGUMENTS' }
Agent cannot modify plan other than session's plan_id (returns 403)
edit_step with stale expected_version returns VERSION_CONFLICT error
VERSION_CONFLICT response includes current_version and expected_version
add_step on non-existent plan returns 404

data_requirements: Test plans in database for tool operations
Valid session tokens for authenticated requests
Multiple test agents for scoping tests
Plans at different versions for optimistic locking tests
